name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash

ds41-halo.summary: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on the 128 GB Lucebox: dense work, hot experts and the drafter on the R9700 (gfx1201), a second expert stack on Strix Halo (gfx1151, carve plus locked host memory), the rest streamed from SSD; the Lucebox placement and router bias from share/deepseek41. One request at a time with --draft; for several at once add --paged-attention --max-concurrency N --ds4-prefill sparse, without --draft

ds41-r9700-gorgon.summary: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on an R9700 (gfx1201) beside a 192 GB Gorgon Halo (gfx1151) with every expert resident: dense work, hot experts and the drafter on the R9700, the other experts on the Gorgon; decoder SWA bounded replay and a pipelined layer-major prefill; pass the expert placement and router bias for the box. One request at a time with --draft; for several at once add --paged-attention --max-concurrency N --ds4-prefill sparse, without --draft
ds41-r9700-gorgon.notes: Prefill: bounded replay, layer-major bands with the residual and Engram on the R9700, both owners joined on the device, the Gorgon's cold FFN of one band under the next band's attention, WMMA for plain ROCmFP2 experts, one arena; the cold owner's input crosses PCIe on a side stream. Prefill attention on the R9700's matrix cores: F16 K/V rows into the WMMA D512 kernels (the gfx1151 set; its indexer and causal-window defaults are slower on gfx1201). Decode and verify: F16 K/V on every lane, split-KV flash (eight splits, short lanes included), fused router and HC collapse (both bit-exact). The rest are the ds41-halo owner and kernel settings.

ds41-gorgon.summary: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on a 192 GB Gorgon Halo (gfx1151) alone, the whole model resident on the iGPU (166 GiB for the 1017 ROCMFP2S file); dense batched prefill, the ROCmFP2 WMMA expert prefill and the fused router and HC collapse on top of the gfx1151 defaults. Not yet measured on a 192 GB board. One request at a time with --draft; for several at once add --paged-attention --max-concurrency N --ds4-prefill sparse, without --draft
ds41-gorgon.notes: On one GPU, dense or sparse prefill loads V4.1 fully resident (the hybrid expert tier comes only with --expert-device or exact prefill), so the expert placement, router bias and --ds4-protected-experts, which act on that tier, are left out. Resident size is the GGUF minus its Engram tables (about 190 GiB, read from the file and never mapped): 166 GiB for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-ROCMFP2S-IM1017.gguf, plus the drafter (4.6 GiB for the Q2K-Q4K one), the KV cache and the prefill buffers (about 4 GiB). The context is 131,072 tokens, half of ds41-r9700-gorgon's, so the KV cache takes about 1.6 GiB and the total stays near the 176 GiB GTT limit of the measured Gorgon; if the model does not load, raise that limit or lower --max-ctx. Of ds41-r9700-gorgon's switches the ROCmFP2 WMMA prefill and the fused router and HC collapse apply on one GPU; the others move work between two GPUs, and bounded replay runs on the hybrid path.

notes: Transcribed from the upstream card's recommended parameters, except max_tokens, which is Lucebox's. Lucebox serves greedy (default_sampling): a request that sets no temperature, or temperature 0, decodes greedily. The sampling block is upstream's recipe, temperature 1.0 and top_p 1.0, for the fields a request leaves out when it sets a temperature above 0. max_tokens is 204800, the context of the 128 GB Lucebox (the ds41-halo profile), since every V4.1 Flash setup shares this card (upstream gives a 1M-token context window and max_tokens of 256K or more). The card states no effort budgets, so the tiers are the ratio defaults of docs/specs/thinking-budget.md section 3.3 for that max_tokens (no complex-problem value, so x-high and max equal high), written out; each is capped at max_ctx minus hard_limit_reply_budget. top_k, min_p and the penalties are absent because the card does not state them. Lucebox's V4.1 Flash GGUFs report general.name 'DeepSeek V4.1 Flash'.
